workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Concatenating makepkg configs without line separators can erase the final job cap or corrupt MAKEFLAGS
leads.consequence: A valid user makepkg.conf with no terminating newline and a final '# comment' comments out the appended MAKEFLAGS assignment. With MAKEFLAGS=-j4 already set, OMARCHY_AUR_BUILD_JOBS=1 produces effective MAKEFLAGS=-j4, restoring the uncapped-four-job case. With no trailing comment, a no-newline MAKEFLAGS assignment merges with the new one into an invalid value and can fail the build. This happens at any adjacent file boundary. The helper's trailing echo masks a failed yay status from omarchy-update; the next update repeats it.

leads.summary: Moving sourced config text to a temporary path breaks relative includes
leads.consequence: A user config that sources a sibling with $(dirname ${BASH_SOURCE[0]}) works when makepkg sources the original file, but after concatenation tries to source the sibling beside the temporary merged file instead. The sibling-sourced settings are absent during the real build; a PKGBUILD depending on them can fail, and the helper's final echo would mask a failed yay status. This repeats on subsequent updates. The appended MAKEFLAGS assignment can make the whole config source return success despite the missing include, so do not rely on makepkg's source_safe to catch it. Configs using their own paths or context can likewise change behaviour. Sourcing once in the preparatory subprocess does not fix the later relocation.
leads.triage: behavioural; Opus follow-up-1 confirmed with review.py run 20260927T141331Z-684c354c and extended (failed source no longer aborts)

leads.summary: Long-form GNU Make job limits survive the -j token filter
leads.consequence: MAKEFLAGS='--jobs=8 --output-sync=recurse' becomes '-j1 --jobs=8 --output-sync=recurse' even with OMARCHY_AUR_BUILD_JOBS=1. GNU Make uses the later --jobs=8, running four independent jobs concurrently in the synthetic fixture instead of one; the explicit override does not constrain make. This recurs on every update until the config changes.

leads.summary: Existing alternate makepkg configs are replaced rather than merged
leads.consequence: A user with yay makepkgconf configured to an alternate file, or an environment MAKEPKG_CONF override, previously built using that file. The updater now unconditionally passes a temporary --makepkgconf copied from /etc and the default user file, omitting the alternate configuration (toolchain settings, build directories, custom options, etc). Yay passes the new path to makepkg --config, and makepkg then skips its automatic user-file lookup for an override. Builds needing the alternate configuration may fail; the helper's trailing echo masks yay failures from the parent, and the next update repeats the same change.

leads.summary: Current quattro base has an unresolved merge conflict at the yay invocation
leads.consequence: GitHub currently marks this PR CONFLICTING/DIRTY against quattro; merge-file marks the yay invocation. Quattro's update now revokes authorization before the AUR step, sets OMARCHY_SUDO_NO_UPDATE=1, passes an explicit no-update sudo wrapper via --sudo/--sudoloop=false, and exits on yay failure. This PR's replacement invocation carries neither flag; resolving in favor of the PR drops the forced wrapper (allowing a different yay-configured sudo command) and makes failed yay calls report success after echo. Preserve current-base security and failure semantics. Reconcile both argv sets and error propagation, then run both tests against the resolved version.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F5; coordinator verified base-tip line and #9467 merge time

leads.summary: Potential root-to-user temp-file permission conflict with open PR #12796
leads.consequence: #12796 proposes running yay as SUDO_USER when updater is root. If its sudo -u handoff is combined after this PR's mktemp, the config file is root-owned mode 0600 and the target user cannot read it for makepkg --config; AUR updates fail (with this PR's helper potentially hiding the failure). Both heads are diverged and the files conflict, so this depends on the as-yet-unresolved integration. Resolve by creating a private config as the build user or safely granting that user access and run the combined code under a sandboxed identity fixture.
leads.triage: hypothesis, matches Opus #12796 note (inferred); not published, combination not runnable

leads.summary: Invalid explicit build-job counts flow into make without validation
leads.consequence: The one-job floor protects only the nproc default. If OMARCHY_AUR_BUILD_JOBS=0 (or a typo such as cat), the updater constructs MAKEFLAGS=-j0 (or -jcat) and sets the same invalid job count for Cargo and CMake. GNU Make exits 2 with 'the -j option requires a positive integer argument'. Yay can fail the build, but the helper's trailing echo reports success to the parent; every subsequent update with the same override repeats the error. Validate a positive integer before building the config, or reject it with a diagnostic.
leads.triage: matches Opus minor note; present since 47a2cc14, outside reassessed claims; not published

leads.summary: The new shell test's missing-system-config skip does not exit
leads.consequence: On a machine without readable /etc/makepkg.conf the test prints a SKIP, but skip() only prints text, and the file keeps running. Production then does not create or pass the temporary config, the yay stub cannot copy it, and line 81 fails. test/shell reports both a skip and a failed suite, on every run. Add exit 0 immediately after skip (as neighboring tests do), or supply a synthetic system config.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up at head `a873e0a3` to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12778#issuecomment-5768750538) and the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12778#issuecomment-5825647454). **Verified:** the merged `makepkg.conf` fixes the reported `MAKEFLAGS="-j4"` case.

The cap still misses the `--jobs=N` spelling. Copying the config text into one temporary file also introduces new build failures and hides config errors. The branch now conflicts with `quattro`.

| Earlier claim | Status at `a873e0a3` |
|---|---|
| Verified priority and job-count behavior | Still holds |
| makepkg configuration can override the Make job count | Resolved for `-jN` configs, still present for `--jobs=N` and `--jobs N` |
| Scope correction (job-count defaults, not a CPU guarantee) | Resolved in the code comment; the PR description still makes the old claim (see the note below) |

**Verified:** with real makepkg 7.1.0 and GNU Make 4.4.1, the reported case (user config `MAKEFLAGS="-j4"`, `OMARCHY_AUR_BUILD_JOBS=1`) now reaches `prepare()` and `build()` as `-j1` and runs 1 concurrent job. `-j4 --output-sync=recurse` becomes `-j1 --output-sync=recurse`. The `~/.makepkg.conf` fallback and an unset `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` also resolve to `-j1`. yay 13.0.1, the version Omarchy ships, passes `--makepkgconf` to every makepkg call as `--config`. yay and the build still run at niceness 15 and best-effort I/O priority 7, the environment values at the yay boundary are unchanged, and the temporary file is removed on exit. The new test passes at this head and fails against both earlier updaters.

### The cap only recognizes the `-jN` spelling

At [`omarchy-update-aur-pkgs:43-50`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/a873e0a374534c0b012276f7424196a2a22aaefd/bin/omarchy-update-aur-pkgs#L43-L50), only words matching `^-j[0-9]*$` are removed, and the selected `-jN` is placed first. GNU Make uses the last job option it sees. Measured with `OMARCHY_AUR_BUILD_JOBS=1` and a synthetic four-job Makefile:

| User config `MAKEFLAGS` | Merge base | This head |
|---|---|---|
| `"-j4"` | 4 jobs | `-j1`: 1 job |
| `"--jobs=4"` | 4 jobs | `-j1 --jobs=4`: 4 jobs |
| `"--jobs 4"` | not run | `-j1 --jobs 4`: 4 jobs |
| `"-j 4"` | 4 jobs, build succeeds | `-j1 4`: Make stops with `No rule to make target '4'`, makepkg exits 4 |

**Impact:** `--jobs=$(nproc)` is the form the [Arch Wiki makepkg page](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Makepkg#Parallel_compilation) suggests, so users who followed it still get their configured job count, even with an explicit override. A `-j 4` config, which built before this PR, now makes Make-based AUR builds fail, because Make treats the leftover `4` as a target.

**Suggested change:** append the selected option after the retained flags instead of before them. At Make level, `-j 4 -j1`, `--jobs=4 -j1`, `--jobs 4 -j1` and `-j4 --output-sync=recurse -j1` each ran 1 job with exit 0. Alternatively, also strip `--jobs[=N]` and a separate number after `-j` or `--jobs`. A patched updater was not run.

### Copying config text into one temporary file changes how makepkg loads it

makepkg sources each config file separately from its own path. At [`omarchy-update-aur-pkgs:52-66`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/a873e0a374534c0b012276f7424196a2a22aaefd/bin/omarchy-update-aur-pkgs#L52-L66), the files are joined with `cat` into a `mktemp` file ending in the `MAKEFLAGS=` line, and makepkg sources that file instead. Measured with real makepkg 7.1.0, comparing the merge base and this head:

| User config | Merge base | This head |
|---|---|---|
| Last line `MAKEFLAGS="-j4"`, no final newline | builds, 4 jobs | merged value `-j4MAKEFLAGS=-j1`: Make rejects the `-j` argument, makepkg exits 4 |
| `MAKEFLAGS="-j4"`, then a last-line comment with no final newline | builds, 4 jobs | appended `MAKEFLAGS` becomes part of the comment: 4 jobs, cap not applied |
| `source "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/other.conf"` | included settings present | `BASH_SOURCE` names the temp file, the include is not found, the build runs without its settings |
| Last line `source /missing/path.conf` | `Failed to source` error, makepkg exits 6 | makepkg exits 0 and builds |

In the last two rows the failure does not stop makepkg: it aborts only when sourcing a config file returns non-zero, and the merged file always ends with a successful assignment. A config file that failed to source and stopped the build before is now accepted.

**Impact:** valid user configs can now fail to build or lose settings, and config errors no longer stop the build. The same joining applies between `/etc/makepkg.conf`, each drop-in and the user file. That boundary was confirmed from source only.

**Suggested change:** write the merged file as `source '<path>' || return` lines for the system file, each drop-in and the user file, followed by the `MAKEFLAGS=` line. Each file then keeps its own path and line boundaries, and a config file that fails to source still aborts makepkg, as it does today. This approach was not run.

### A custom makepkg config is replaced

The merged file always starts from `/etc/makepkg.conf` and the default user file. makepkg otherwise honors `MAKEPKG_CONF`, and `--config` overrides it. With `MAKEPKG_CONF` pointing to a custom file that sets `-j2` and a marker variable, the merge base built with that file (2 jobs, marker set). This head ignored it (`-j1`, marker unset). yay reads its own config before the command line, so a `makepkgconf` saved in yay's settings is also replaced by `--makepkgconf`. The yay part was confirmed from yay 13.0.1 source only.

**Impact:** users who keep build settings in an alternate makepkg config lose them during `omarchy update`.

**Suggested change:** skip the merged config when `MAKEPKG_CONF` or a yay `makepkgconf` is set (or start from that file), or note the limitation in the updater comment.

### Other notes

**Base conflict:** the branch conflicts with `quattro` in `bin/omarchy-update-aur-pkgs`. [#9467](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/9467), merged after this commit was pushed, changed the same line to `yay "${sudo_options[@]}" -Sua ... || exit 1`, with a no-update sudo wrapper. A resolution needs to keep both the sudo options and `|| exit 1`, as well as this PR's `nice`/`ionice`, environment values and `--makepkgconf`. One such resolution passed this PR's new test and the base's `update-hook-security-test.sh` (all 23 checks, matching the base control).

**Optional test improvement:** in `test/shell.d/aur-update-jobs-test.sh:9`, `skip` only prints a line, so the test keeps running. With `/etc/makepkg.conf` absent (simulated in copies of the updater and test), it printed the SKIP line, then failed `the updater hands yay a merged makepkg.conf`, and the harness listed the file as both skipped and failed. Other whole-file skips in the repository follow `skip` with `exit 0`.

**Documentation note:** the updated code comment addresses the earlier scope correction, but the PR description still says the change caps parallelism "so foreground work always keeps half the CPU". Its Testing section also says "unchanged yay arguments", which no longer holds now that `--makepkgconf` is added.

---

**Test scope:** head `a873e0a374534c0b012276f7424196a2a22aaefd`, compared with the first commit `47a2cc14` and merge base `8f324c90`, and checked for conflicts against `quattro` at `7e8d35ef`. Real makepkg 7.1.0 and GNU Make 4.4.1 ran synthetic PKGBUILDs through the unmodified updater. yay was replaced by a stub that passes the config to makepkg as yay 13.0.1's source does. Source was read for pacman 7.1.0 and yay 13.0.1. No real AUR package, Cargo, CMake or Ninja build, and no desktop-responsiveness measurement. The full `./test/shell` suite was not re-run.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
